assertions.requirement: The runner's K3s server is the cluster's cluster record, written by the API before it serves with the installer-kind connection (a cluster-admin ServiceAccount token plus the server CA, as bootstrap mints it) and the kube-system identity the fixture observed itself; the listed record must carry that identity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/api-child.ts: recordSelf before serving; substrates/local-cluster/environment.ts: ClusterLocalEnvironment waits for the record to list Ready and compares its identity; substrates/local-cluster/cluster-host.ts: LocalClusterHost, publishedKubeconfig and mintInstallerConnection.

assertions.requirement: A hard API-process replacement on the same state root keeps the cluster record: the relaunched API lists the cluster Running under the same Kubernetes identity, and the K3s server is still running.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/environment.ts: replaceController crashes and relaunches api-child.ts on the same state root, clusterIntact; contracts/cluster-local.ts: ClusterLocalContract.run.

assertions.requirement: A Helm-managed API built from this tree, naming its chart published to a registry beside K3s and installed with an older inline chart that lacks the pods/log rule (what an upgrade from a release before 0.1.68 leaves) and selects the management label the Node sets itself, switches the HelmChart to its own digest-pinned OCI chart at start: its ServiceAccount gains pods/log, the HelmChart names that chart with no inline content, and the one replacement API Pod runs Ready on node-restriction.kubernetes.io/anycloud-management, which create and api upgrade set, finds its chart current and is neither replaced nor restarted.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/hosted-chart.ts: proveHostedChartRepair, called by contracts/cluster-local.ts after the API restart.
